---
title: |
  Surprises in\
  time series analysis
author: Rob J Hyndman
date: 26 October 2026
url: robjhyndman.com/uconn2026
abstract: >-
  I will present a statistical framework for identifying anomalies in three time series settings: unusual observations within a single historical series, unusual series within a large collection, and real-time surveillance of incoming data streams.
  In each case, anomalies are identified using a probabilistic approach based on 'surprisal values' --- equal to minus the log (conditional) density of each observation --- with extreme value theory used to model the tail of the surprisal distribution and avoid strong parametric assumptions.
  The methods will be illustrated using the weird package for R, with examples including French and US mortality rates, and pharmaceutical sales.

## Surprisal probabilities

::: {.alertblock}
The probability of an observation at least as unlikely as $y_t$ under density $f$:

$$
  p_t = \mathbb{P}\big(f(Y) \le f(y_t)\big), \qquad Y \sim f
$$
:::

```{r}
#| label: fig_sp
#| results: asis

files <- tar_read(fig_sp_png)
cat("\n::: {.r-stack .r-stretch}\n")
for (step in seq_along(files)) {
  cat(if (step == 1) "\n::: {.step}\n" else "\n::: {.fragment}\n")
  cat("![](", files[step], "){width=1800}\n", sep = "")
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
cat("\n:::\n")
```

::: {.absolute .fragment top="300" left="740" width="480"}
::::: {.alertblock}
An observation is an **anomaly with respect to $f$** if $p_t < \alpha$.
:::::
:::

## Surprisals {.small}

::: {.alertblock}
The **surprisal** of an observation $y_t$ under density $f$ is $s_t = -\log f(y_t)$
:::

Surprisals are already familiar:

::: {.cards}
::::: {.block}
[Forecasting]{.block-title}

Log score for evaluating density forecasts
:::::

::::: {.block}
[Information theory]{.block-title}

Expected surprisal = entropy
:::::

::::: {.block}
[Likelihood]{.block-title}

Sum of surprisals = [$-$log likelihood]{style="white-space: nowrap"}
:::::
:::

::: {.fragment}
Let $S = -\log f(Y)$ where $Y \sim f$, and $G(s) = \mathbb{P}(S \le s)$.\
[Then $p_t = \mathbb{P}(S \ge s_t) = 1 - G(s_t)$.]{.fragment}
:::

::: {.fragment}
An anomaly is an extreme value of the surprisal distribution.
:::

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::::: {.block .fragment}
[$f$may be complicated]{.block-title}

Multimodal, multivariate or conditional: $G$ is still a univariate distribution on $\mathbb{R}$.
:::::

::::: {.alertblock .fragment}
[$f$may be wrong]{.block-title}

The [upper tail]{.alert} probabilities of $G$ can be estimated using EVT.
:::::
:::

## Surprisals have GPD tails

::: {.block}
[Theorem: surprisals have Generalised Pareto Distribution (GPD) tails]{.block-title}

If the upper tail of $S = -\log f(Y)$ is smooth, then as the threshold $u$ grows,

<!-- panache-ignore-format-start -->
$$
  \mathbb{P}\left( \frac{S - u}{a(u)} \le y \;\middle|\; S > u \right)
  \longrightarrow
  \begin{cases}
    1 - (1 + \xi y)^{-1/\xi}, & \xi > 0,\\
    1 - e^{-y}, & \xi = 0.
  \end{cases}
$$
<!-- panache-ignore-format-end -->
:::

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::::: {.block .fragment}
[Exponential moment: $\mathbb{E}\,e^{\lambda S} < \infty$]{.block-title}

$\xi = 0$: exponential tail\
e.g., Normal $f$
:::::

::::: {.block .fragment}
[Only polynomial moments: $\mathbb{E}\,S^q < \infty$]{.block-title}

$0 < \xi \le 1/q$: Pareto tail\
e.g., Normal $f$, but $t$ data
:::::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::::: {.alertblock}
Conditions are on $S$, not $Y$: they hold [even if $f$ is wrong]{.alert}.
:::::
:::

## Univariate experiment

What happens when the distribution used to compute surprisals is mis-specified?

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::::: {.block}
[Data: Normal]{.block-title}

- 1000 observations from a N(0,1) distribution
- Surprisals computed using a t(4) distribution.
- Estimate surprisal probabilities using N(0,1), t(4), GPD
:::::

::::: {.block}
[Data: t(4)]{.block-title}

- 1000 observations from a t(4) distribution
- Surprisals computed using a N(0,1) distribution.
- Estimate surprisal probabilities using N(0,1), t(4), GPD
:::::
:::

## Hampel identifier {.nostretch}

````{r}
#| label: fig_hampel
#| results: asis

# Stages: series; first window; window tracing the median (video);
# difference; Normal. Fragment indices match the equations and bullets below.
files <- tar_read(fig_hampel_png)
video <- htmltools::tagAppendAttributes(
  video_tag(tar_read(hampel_video)),
  style = "width:100%"
)
cat("\n::: {.r-stack}\n\n")
cat("![](", files[1], "){width=100%}\n\n", sep = "")
cat("::: {.fragment fragment-index=\"1\"}\n")
cat("![](", files[2], "){width=100%}\n:::\n\n", sep = "")
cat(
  "::: {.fragment fragment-index=\"2\"}\n```{=html}\n",
  as.character(video),
  "\n```\n:::\n\n",
  sep = ""
)
for (i in 3:4) {
  cat("::: {.fragment fragment-index=\"", i + 1, "\"}\n", sep = "")
  cat("![](", files[i], "){width=100%}\n:::\n\n", sep = "")
}
cat(":::\n")
````

```{=html}
<script>
// Play a video when the fragment containing it is shown; rewind it when hidden
window.addEventListener("load", function () {
  function videos(e) {
    return e.fragments.flatMap(function (f) {
      return Array.from(f.querySelectorAll("video"));
    });
  }
  Reveal.on("fragmentshown", function (e) {
    videos(e).forEach(function (v) {
      v.currentTime = 0;
      v.play();
    });
  });
  Reveal.on("fragmenthidden", function (e) {
    videos(e).forEach(function (v) {
      v.pause();
      v.currentTime = 0;
    });
  });
});
</script>
```

::: {.columns}
::::: {.column .math-left width="52%"}
::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}
$$
  m_t = \text{median}(y_{t-w}, \dots, y_{t+w})
$$
:::::::

::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}
$$
  a_t = \text{median}(|y_{t-w} - m_t|, \dots, |y_{t+w} - m_t|)
$$
:::::::

::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}
- Anomaly if $|y_t - m_t| > ka_t$
:::::::
:::::
::::: {.column width="48%"}
::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="5"}
- Implicit model: $y_t \sim \text{N}(m_t, \sigma_t^2)$ with $\sigma_t = a_t/0.6745$
:::::::
::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="6"}
- Better: compute surprisals under Normal, with probabilities from GPD
:::::::
:::::
:::

## Surprisals from an STL decomposition {.small}

::: {.columns}
::::: {.column width="34%"}
Local medians fail with seasonality.

::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="1"}
Replace by a better signal estimate for each age group:
:::::::

::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="2"}
- STL: $y_t = T_t + S_t + R_t$ (Cleveland et al., 1990; Bandara\ et al., 2025)
:::::::

::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="3"}
- $a_t$: robust estimate of $\{R_t\}$ stdev, separately for each age group
:::::::

::::::: {.fragment fragment-index="4"}
- $e_t = R_t / a_t$; surprisals under N(0,1), probabilities from GPD
:::::::
:::::
::::: {.column width="66%"}
::::::: {.fragment .code-steps fragment-index="2" data-steps="3-5:3,6-7:4,8-9:5,10:6"}
<!-- panache-ignore-format-start -->
```{r}
#| label: stl-stmf
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

stmf_scores <- us_stmf |>
  model(stl = STL(Mortality)) |> augment() |>
  group_by(`Age group`) |>
  mutate(
    a = robustbase::s_Qn(.resid),
    e = .resid / a
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(prob = surprisals_prob(e, "gpd", distribution = dist_normal())) |>
  arrange(prob)
```
<!-- panache-ignore-format-end -->
:::::::

`````{r}
#| label: stmf_scores_print
#| results: asis

# Each table adds the columns computed by the code revealed at the same step;
# all but the last are hidden when the next one appears
tables <- tar_read(stmf_scores_steps)
cat("\n::: {.r-stack .output-steps}\n\n")
for (k in seq_along(tables)) {
  last <- k == length(tables)
  cat(
    "::: {.fragment",
    if (!last) " .current-visible",
    " fragment-index=\"",
    k + 1,
    "\"}\n",
    "::::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}\n````\n",
    sep = ""
  )
  cat(capture.output(print(tables[[k]])), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n````\n:::::\n:::\n\n")
}
cat(":::\n")
`````
:::::
:::

```{=html}
<script>
// Reveal code lines in steps: data-steps="4-6:3,7:4" makes lines 4-6 a
// fragment with index 3 and line 7 a fragment with index 4. A pipe ending
// the line before each step appears with that step, so the last visible line
// never ends in a dangling pipe. Runs before Reveal is initialised, so the new
// fragments are picked up.
document.querySelectorAll(".code-steps[data-steps]").forEach(function (div) {
  var lines = div.querySelectorAll("pre code > span[id]");
  div.dataset.steps.split(",").forEach(function (step) {
    var parts = step.split(":");
    var range = parts[0].split("-").map(Number);
    for (var i = range[0]; i <= (range[1] || range[0]); i++) {
      lines[i - 1].classList.add("fragment");
      lines[i - 1].dataset.fragmentIndex = parts[1];
    }
    var prev = lines[range[0] - 2];
    var pipe = prev && Array.from(prev.querySelectorAll("span.sc")).pop();
    if (pipe && pipe.textContent === "|>" && prev.textContent.trimEnd().endsWith("|>")) {
      pipe.classList.add("fragment");
      pipe.dataset.fragmentIndex = parts[1];
    }
  });
});
</script>
```

<script>
// Play the zoom when arriving from the previous slide; otherwise (or once it
// has finished) show the interactive plot
window.addEventListener("load", function () {
  var slide = document.getElementById("us-zoom");
  var video = slide.querySelector(".zoom-video video");
  video.addEventListener("ended", function () {
    slide.classList.add("zoom-done");
  });
  Reveal.on("slidechanged", function (e) {
    if (e.currentSlide !== slide) return;
    var prev = e.previousSlide && Reveal.getIndices(e.previousSlide).h;
    if (prev === Reveal.getIndices(slide).h - 1) {
      slide.classList.remove("zoom-done");
      video.currentTime = 0;
      video.play();
    } else {
      slide.classList.add("zoom-done");
    }
  });
});
</script>

## Kernel density surprisals {.small}

::: {.block}
[KDE]{.block-title}

$$
  \boldsymbol{y}_{i} \in \mathbb{R}^d, \quad \hat{f}(\boldsymbol{y})
  = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^n |\boldsymbol{H}|^{-1/2} K\big(\boldsymbol{H}^{-1/2}(\boldsymbol{y} - \boldsymbol{y}_i)\big)
$$
:::

- $K$: spherically symmetric kernel; $\boldsymbol{H}$: $d \times d$ bandwidth matrix.
- Each observation inflates its own density estimate: use leave-one-out.

::: {.fragment}
::::: {.block}
[LOO KDE values]{.block-title}

$$
  \hat{f}_{-i}(\boldsymbol{y}_i)
  = \frac{1}{n - 1} \big( n \hat{f}(\boldsymbol{y}_i) - |\boldsymbol{H}|^{-1/2} K(\boldsymbol{0}) \big)
$$

- Surprisals $s_i = -\log \hat{f}_{-i}(\boldsymbol{y}_i)$; probabilities from the GPD.
:::::
:::

## Surprisal probabilities as p-values

::: {.incremental}
- If $f_{i,t+1|t}$ is the true forecast density, and the surprisal distribution is continuous, then
  $$
    p_{i,t+1} \mid y_{i,1},\dots,y_{i,t} \sim \text{U}(0,1)
  $$
  so the $p_{i,t}$ are iid U(0,1) over $t$.
- Thresholding at $\alpha$ gives a false alarm rate of $\alpha$ per series per period.
- Model updated each period, so a level shift is flagged when it happens, then becomes the "new normal".
- ETS: Gaussian forecast distributions, so $p_{i,t+1}$ is a two-sided $z$-test on the one-step forecast error.
:::

## A first iteration: $t = 36$

```{r}
#| label: pbsfc
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

pbs_fc <- pbs |>
  filter(t <= 36) |>
  group_by_key() |>
  filter(cumsum(Scripts) > 0, n() >= 36) |>
  ungroup() |>
  model(ets = ETS(Scripts)) |>
  forecast(h = 1)
```

```{r}
#| label: pbsfc_print

tar_read(pbs_fc) |> print(n = 7, width = Inf)
```

## Surveillance across several series {.small}

Some events affect many series at once: mildly unusual in each, very unusual together.

- $M_t$: number of series monitored at time $t$
- $N_t$: number of series with $p_{i,t} < 0.001$
- Independent series: $N_t \sim \text{Binomial}(M_t, \pi)$
- Surprisal probability: $\mathbb{P}(N_t \ge n_t)$

::: {.fragment}
- $\pi = 0.001$ if forecast densities correct
- ETS forecast densities too narrow: actual rate is `r sprintf("%.3f", mean(pbs_scores$prob < 0.001, na.rm = TRUE))`
- Solution: estimate $\pi$ from all previous months
:::

<script>
// On slides with class "code-steps", show the n-th ".step-output" block when n
// code-highlight steps have been revealed, so outputs follow the code
window.addEventListener("load", function () {
  function update() {
    document.querySelectorAll("section.code-steps").forEach(function (slide) {
      var step = slide.querySelectorAll("code.fragment.visible").length;
      slide.querySelectorAll(".step-output").forEach(function (out, i) {
        out.classList.toggle("current", i === step);
      });
    });
  }
  ["ready", "slidechanged", "fragmentshown", "fragmenthidden"].forEach(function (e) {
    Reveal.on(e, update);
  });
  update();
});
</script>
```
